subject: physical-education
essentialQuestion: How do I find the flaw in my own movement without anyone filming me?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of critical features of a movement and what each contributes in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe self-observation by feel, mirror, shadow, and outcome pattern using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply diagnosing from the result rather than from an image in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it; correct it and explain why.
Connect transfer of a corrected pattern into an activity with plateaus and what to change when progress stops and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Choose one skill, identify its critical features, diagnose the learner’s own limiting feature from outcome evidence, design and run the corrective practice, and document the change.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Any skill the learner can perform, in any range or position, is a valid choice, including a mobility-aid skill or a seated skill. Analysis may be described, drawn, or tabled.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
